channel.title: The GW Hatchet - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The GW Hatchet (gwhatchet.com)

item.title: Students blast GW Law for declining to disinvite ICE from public interest career fair
item.description: Students condemned GW Law officials' decision not to revoke U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement's invitation to a public interest career fair on Friday after more than 1,000 students signed a petition calling on officials to bar them.

item.title: Milken partners with Washington Performing Arts to bring music, dance to senior care facility
item.description: Milken Institute School of Public Health students will help design and evaluate weekly dance and music sessions for seniors at Ingleside at Rock Creek, a retirement community in D.C.

item.title: Students with GW-employed parents blend home and school life on campus
item.description: For many students, college means putting distance between home and family. For senior Bella Costantino, home is just a short walk across campus — up the steps of the University Honors Program building, where her mother works.

item.title: WMATA officials begin upgrades to Foggy Bottom Metro escalators
item.description: Washington Metropolitan Area Transit Authority officials began renovations expected to last for the next five months on two Foggy Bottom-GWU Metro station escalators, upgrading motors to increase energy efficiency and reliability.

item.title: From Trump to GW administrative shakeups, The Hatchet looks back at 2016’s biggest stories
item.description: From President Donald Trump to high leadership turnover, some things never change. Take a look at some of The Hatchet’s biggest stories of 2016.

item.title: March for Life draws thousands to DC as Trump enters second year of presidency
item.description: Thousands of anti-abortion activists rallied on the National Mall and marched through Downtown D.C., condemning abortion and calling on the federal government to take more action to restrict access to reproductive care.

item.title: GW Hospital resumes bargaining with service workers union eight years after unfair labor petition
item.description: GW Hospital announced Thursday it has begun open bargaining with a service workers union, more than a year after the National Labor Relations Board ruled the hospital violated labor laws by bargaining in bad faith.

item.title: GW turns to virtual power purchase agreement to meet carbon goals without REC reliance
item.description: GW entered into a power purchase agreement to support solar energy development, which will allow them to scrap their reliance on renewable energy credits they purchased to reach 2025 sustainability goals while still getting energy from their local power grid.

item.title: Georgetown cat cafe employees move to unionize over safety, workplace concerns
item.description: On this episode of Getting to the Bottom of It, Crumbs & Whiskers employees talk to co-hosts Max Porter and Lizzie Jensen and reporter Maddie Flesch about their efforts to unionize and what led to the decision. This podcast was hosted and produced by Lizzie Jensen and Max Porter. Aulx Studio

item.title: Men’s basketball falls in 79-76 heartbreaker to ranked Saint Louis
item.description: Men's basketball fell 79-76 to ranked Saint Louis on Tuesday night on a late 3-pointer.
